ownerListeningNotes.baa: Older sounds like baa; newer sounds like bah and gives a different-accent impression.
ownerListeningNotes.meem: Newer stretches the middle and sounds subdued; older sounds more excited.
ownerListeningNotes.overall: Softer, more feminine, teacher-like, brighter and more engaged; not deep or neutral.
ownerListeningNotes.march: March sounds better, but slightly too high pitched; owner describes its delivery as lacking modesty and sounding like someone trying to sound attractive. It is closer, not approved.
ownerListeningNotes.composedTeacher: Getting better, but feels slightly dragged out and less smooth. Closer, not yet approved.

interpretation.baa: Reported vowel/articulation mismatch, not a confirmed regional-accent identification. The input remains بَاءْ in both recordings.
interpretation.meem: Reported timing and expression mismatch. The measured longer active region and narrower pitch variation support timing/prosody differences, but do not independently certify the vowel pronunciation.
interpretation.limits: No specific accent, human identity or emotional/mental state is inferred. The synthetic delivery is being described perceptually.
interpretation.march: A subjective report about the synthetic performance, not an inference of intent or personality. Breathiness or pitch glides are possible style features to reduce, not a diagnosed acoustic cause.

desiredDirection: Warm, composed and gently encouraging classroom teacher. Natural feminine middle register, clear steady tone, understated expression, small pitch variation. Preserve accurate Arabic articulation and long vowels.
acceptanceChecks: Match the approved reference pronunciation and vowel quality, not just the approximate pitch.
Preserve letter-name spelling and correct vowel-length distinctions; do not shorten a long vowel merely to make a clip quicker.
Warm, attentive and composed classroom delivery, with understated expression; no exaggerated high register, breathy or sing-song performance, and no deep or flat delivery.
Natural vowel duration without drawn-out holds, artificial stretching or a heavy falling ending.
Stable vocal character across letters, syllables and words; compare against actual approved references.
No repetition, additional sounds, static or low-frequency artifacts.
Smooth continuous letter-name delivery at a natural pace; preserve correct long vowels without extra holds or pauses inside a name.
notASolution: Respelling Arabic to force an English-sounding baa/bah reading
